QUALIFY-ONLY, ZERO FIXES -- the same posture as NFRA_DEPLOYCENSUS: a card names a defect and its OWNER, it does not remediate, and a finding is never a dispatch. THE END GOAL IS NOT THE CARDS: Andrew, verbatim -- 'the end goal is to basically develop a mechanical process around the materialization and tracking of c3.i'. The four-stage identity pipeline (affinity compilation -> similarity network fusion -> identity -> succession) cannot be built on substrate whose grain, state, coverage, key space and failure modes are unknown, and six separate id-space defects were measured in one day while trying. WAVE 1 SUBJECTS (bounded, known): C0, C1, C2, C3.i-as-built, D1, D2, D3, and whatever underlies comp-similar. WAVE 2 IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED: questions 1 and 4 of every wave-1 card NAME the generators and storage locations, so the wave-2 subject list falls out of wave-1 output rather than being enumerated up front. SEPARATE STANDING DELIVERABLE: a graph-object manifest -- what graph stores exist, which are heavy/authoritative vs light/traversable projections, and each tagged to its generator -- assembled from the projection_of lineage the cards carry. Andrew's concern, verbatim: 'something that is very concerning to me is not having a clear manifest of what graph objects exist and where involved in this process'.

No lane could have avoided it while following the schema; the defect was the field type. || ⛔ ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE, owed at the wave boundary and STRONGER than the joinable_ref fix it supersedes in scope: 2.0.0_SA_COO~X's tension proof (73329) shows NO DEDUP HEURISTIC ON THESE FIELDS CAN BE CORRECT -- a key strict enough to catch false splits MERGES kuzu_nessie_db with s3://opal-estate-report/kuzu_nessie_db (two distinct objects, 82.5MB local vs 51.0MB in-bucket, corroborated independently at the CTO~X seat), and a key loose enough to keep them apart leaves the splits. THE L0 MANIFEST MUST BECOME THE REGISTRY -- minting part_id per part, with cards REFERENCING a registered part_id rather than a free-text name. Same L1-entity-spine problem one layer down, which is why it recurs: free-text names have been asked to do an identity registry's job. All four TOs rewritten @b918167857. THE GENERALIZATION: this is the SAME DEFECT as sysi:{domain}:{sha1(anchor_node_id)} and as the 51-vs-43 spelling collisions. ALL THREE ARE DERIVED IDENTITIES -- an id computed from something MUTABLE (a list position, an anchor resource, a free-text spelling) rather than MINTED ONCE AND TRACKED. Position is just the cheapest mutable thing to derive from. A registry that mints and tracks closes all three; no amount of care closes any of them, because in every case the derived id RESOLVES CLEANLY while meaning something else.
